title: Validating a mechanistic EEG generator against real data: the Jansen-Rit neural mass reproduces a real alpha rhythm

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb), subject S001, run R02 (eyes closed), channel O1
dataset.record: S001R02, occipital O1 @ 160 Hz, 61 s eyes-closed baseline; real alpha peak 10.0 Hz, relative alpha power 0.67
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51:1034-1043. PhysioNet doi:10.13026/C28G6P (ODC-BY 1.0).

proposition: This is a SIMULATION-VALIDATION case: does the mechanistic Jansen-Rit neural-mass model (a single cortical column of coupled neural populations) reproduce a REAL EEG's alpha rhythm, not just oscillate plausibly on its own? A real eyes-closed occipital EEG has a 10.0 Hz alpha peak carrying 67% of its 1-40 Hz power. The generic Jansen-Rit column emits alpha at 10.75 Hz; scaling its membrane time constants x0.96 to the real alpha frequency puts the model's peak at 10.0 Hz, and in BOTH the real recording and the model alpha is the dominant band. A bare cortical column OVER-concentrates power in alpha (relative alpha 0.99 vs the real 0.67); adding a physiological 1/f (aperiodic) background of fitted amplitude (x1.8 the oscillation SD) spreads power off the peak and brings the model's relative alpha to 0.65, now matching the real 0.67. Both the emergent rhythm AND its spectral shape are VALIDATED against reality, distinct from being merely verified on synthetic data.

claims.statement: dominant frequency of the real eyes-closed occipital EEG (Hz), in the alpha band
personalised Jansen-Rit dominant frequency (Hz), fit to the real alpha peak
relative alpha power of the real EEG (alpha / 1-40 Hz)
relative alpha power of the bare Jansen-Rit column (no 1/f background) -- OVER-concentrated
relative alpha power of the personalised Jansen-Rit EEG WITH a fitted 1/f background -- now matching the real value
fitted 1/f (aperiodic) background amplitude (multiple of the oscillation SD)

validation.reference: A mechanistic EEG generator is VALIDATED (not merely verified) if it reproduces the EMERGENT RHYTHM of a real recording: (1) the ALPHA PEAK FREQUENCY (the dominant spectral peak, in the 8-13 Hz band), and (2) the ALPHA-DOMINANT spectral shape (alpha is the largest conventional band in both real and model). Jansen-Rit (Jansen & Rit 1995) is the canonical neural-mass EEG model; matching its membrane time constants to the real alpha frequency and comparing the resulting spectrum to a real eyes-closed occipital EEG must satisfy both.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb S001R02 (PhysioNet), occipital channel O1, 61 s eyes-closed baseline @ 160 Hz
validation.note: This is the L4 (validation-against-reality) tier of simulation validity, distinct from synthetic-data recovery, which only VERIFIES the estimator. The mechanistic Jansen-Rit column reproduces the real EEG's emergent alpha rhythm AND its spectral shape: the generic model already peaks at 10.75 Hz (within 0.75 Hz of the real 10.0 Hz), and scaling its membrane time constants x0.96 to the real alpha frequency matches it exactly at 10.0 Hz, with alpha the dominant band in both real and model. A bare single cortical column OVER-concentrates power in alpha (relative alpha 0.99 vs the real 0.67), because a real scalp channel carries a broadband 1/f (aperiodic) background that one column does not; adding that physiological 1/f background (jansenRit(aperiodic=), amplitude fit to the record) spreads power off the peak and brings the model's relative alpha to 0.65, matching the real 0.67 -- so the match now covers both the alpha peak and the broadband spectral shape, resolving the earlier over-concentration. Honest scope: (1) what is validated is the RHYTHM and its spectral shape -- the alpha peak frequency, band dominance and relative alpha power -- NOT the exact EEG waveform, since EEG is stochastic and a neural-mass model reproduces the spectral rhythm, not the sample path; (2) a single channel (O1), a single subject (S001), eyes-closed resting only -- no montage, task or cross-subject range; (3) two scalars are calibrated to this record -- the membrane-time-constant scale (to the alpha frequency) and the 1/f amplitude (to the relative alpha) -- so the aperiodic background is FIT to the recording, not predicted from the mechanism, and its spectral slope is the resting-EEG default. This case lives with PhysioTwin and migrates to public PhysioRecipes.

open_questions.q: The 1/f background that reproduces the broadband spectrum is here FIT to the record (its amplitude tuned to the relative alpha); coupling several columns (Jansen-Rit networks) would let that broadband aperiodic floor EMERGE from the mechanism instead. Validating across many subjects, channels and eyes-open/closed states would then quantify the model's domain of applicability. Documented, not escalated.
